ranges.quote: So you're doom scrolling TikTok, and it seems to never end. Now, instead of loading everything ahead of time, TikTok does something really smart here. Pay attention.
ranges.reason: Only take of the hook. ASR boxes 'attention.' out to 12.28; find_dead_air puts the acoustic end at 9.17, so cutting at 9.25 removes 3.03s of room tone that padding off the ASR end would have preserved. The 1.03s beat inside ('here.' -> 'Pay') is rhetorical and kept.

ranges.quote: Now, here's the problem. Loading all ten thousand posts up front would burn data, memory, and make the app freeze before showing anything.
ranges.reason: Single clean take. ASR end and acoustic end agree at 23.68.

ranges.quote: So we lazy load. Only fetch what's about to enter the screen as you scroll near the bottom. The app quietly requests the next batch.
ranges.reason: Single clean take, continuous across the 0.52s breath at 29.48->30.00.

ranges.quote: In order to grab the next batch reliably, we use cursor pagination. Hey, give me items after this ID instead of page numbers, which break when new posts arrive mid-scroll.
ranges.reason: Take 2 of 2. Take 1 (35.12) aborts at 37.14 on 'reliably...'. Cut at 51.95 lands 110ms after 'mid-scroll.' with 630ms of clearance before 'Items'.

ranges.quote: Items above the screen can even be unloaded to save memory. The feed feels infinite because the work is spread across your scrolling.
ranges.reason: Contiguous with NEW_COMPONENT in the source but kept as its own range so the unload/recycle idea can carry its own overlay.

ranges.quote: Now, here's the AI angle. Which batch you get isn't random. A recommendation model decides what to lazy load. So loading and ranking happen together.
ranges.reason: Take 6 of 8 and the tightest complete read. Takes at 62.34/71.60/85.22/90.64/102.48/110.08/134.34 all abort. The remaining complete take (141.40) drags: 'here's' is boxed 541ms vs 170ms here, and it leaves a 330ms hole after 'angle.' where this take runs straight through at 40ms.

ranges.quote: Load what they see, not what they might see. Next episode, we'll look at how sign-in with Google works.
ranges.reason: Only complete take. Runs continuously into the next-episode tease with a natural 0.66s beat between them.

_windows_note: Output-timeline windows on render.py's real 24fps extract grid: each segment's rendered duration is ceil((end-start)*24)/24, not the raw source span. Verified against rendered clips where measurable. Overlay start_in_output values are derived from THESE numbers.
_overlay_gap_audit: Gaps >= 0.5s are deliberate returns to the talking head (ep13 shipped 1.0-6.7s gaps at 49-54% coverage). Anything shorter is closed to exactly zero, per rule 12 -- a sub-half-second hole reads as a bare-footage flash, not a breath. EP19 tradeoff->payoff is contiguous for exactly this reason: its beats butt up against each other and a 0.3s gap would have landed on the punchline.
_hook_lead_note: slot_hook starts at 0.000 on purpose. Its beat also starts at 0.000, so the usual >=0.25s lead would mean waiting on the title card. This slot is a transparent/right-side format specifically so it can run SIMULTANEOUSLY with the title (rule 10) -- making it opaque would delay its content until 2.766 and the beat's idea would land late, which is the EP7 hook mistake. The content is ambient (a scrolling column / a streaming URL), not a claim that needs the narration to establish it first.
_zoom_note: Gradual CENTERED zoom on the talking head. focal (540,960) = exact frame centre, not render.py's eye-line default. Direction alternates per segment so each range starts at the scale the previous one ended on -- the drift is continuous across every cut instead of snapping back to 1.0 at each edit. Magnitude capped at 4.5%: the overlays were placed against measured face positions with clearances as tight as 40px, and a centered zoom displaces a point by distance_from_centre*(Z-1), so 4.5% costs the tightest one ~13px while 12% would cost it ~35px and push graphics into the face.
